summary.severityChanges: none. Every re-weighed entry keeps its prior severity, with the premises updated. L-23's documented 'V2 wired => MEDIUM' trigger fired, and it was re-rated on the probe evidence instead of being escalated automatically.
borderline: DEDUP-18-04 (QA vs drop; owner previously rejected MEV framings)
summary.newObservation: OBS-18-01 (see below): owner-driven exit of the revoked OLD minter's 58% USDe position while the vault is below par moves the commingled loss onto StableStakerV2. That inverts the minter-cushion premise. It is not a code defect, and it is surfaced for human triage as a potential Law-3 footgun. No finding was minted.

premisesApplied: StableStakerV2 0xA6d3...B58F LIVE and the only REDEEMING client of each strategy. V1 holds 0 principal. The OLD minter 0x435B (58% of USDe) and the new minter 0x9485 are non-redeeming cushions. The minter-cushion socialisation premise therefore HOLDS on the live client set.
V2 emits Antimatter redeemable into unbacked phUSD, so phUSD minted for a shortfall, or any over-credit to V2, is real dilution and not opportunity cost.
Over- or under-payment of externally derived yield to a pot is opportunity cost.

V2 exit paths verified in stable-staker/src/src/StableStakerV2.sol: withdraw/autoAnnihilate pass guardUnderwater=true (_routeExit :1315). emergencyWithdraw (:695-711) and initiateMigration (:780-790) pass false, so V2 CAN exit while the vault is underwater, either per user or as a full-position migration.

classifications.change: none (premise re-weighed: V2 live, I8 reachability path)

classification.assetImpact: No asset moves incorrectly because of the early return. The harm is state and signalling: Phase-2 totalWithdrawal emits WithdrawalExecuted and resets the two-phase state, but it moves nothing while principal stays booked. The co-client's unbacked principal in the I8 replay comes from the enabling cap-bind (the commingled loss lands on the last exiters), not from L-28.
attackPath: 1. The vault suffers a loss that pushes V below D.
2. A single exit whose request exceeds the NAV of ALL strategy shares cap-binds and takes every share while debiting only its own principal.
3. The remaining clients keep booked principal backed by 0 shares.
4. The owner's totalWithdrawal(remaining client) Phase-2 hits `totalShares == 0` and returns silently as 'executed'.
classification.likelihood: very low on the live client set. A cap-bind needs the exiter's principal >= the NAV of the whole position. With live shares of OLD minter 58% / V2 41% / new minter <1%, the loss needed is >= 42% (minter exits first) or >= 58.6% (V2 initiateMigration exits first). The 3% loss in the I8 replay needs an exiter holding >97% of principal, and no live client does. Individual V2 emergencyWithdraws are far too small to cap-bind.
classification.whoIsTheFirstExiter: (a) V2 on the voluntary path: blocked by _isUnderwater. (b) V2 via emergencyWithdraw/initiateMigration: unguarded. Here V2 is the WINNER (made whole) and the non-redeeming minter absorbs the loss, which is the intended cushion direction. (c) An owner-driven exit of the OLD minter: then V2 is the victim. But the V2 loss is the realised vault loss, which L-28's no-op neither causes nor deepens. Also, totalWithdrawal is onlyOwner and redeems to the owner, and V2 never calls it, so no V2 user claim is routed through the silent no-op.
classification.assumptions: The live client set stays as observed at block 26286995. Owner non-malicious.
classification.externalRequirements: A loss event >= 42% of the commingled USDe position (an extraordinary event)

classifications.justification: With V2 live this STAYS LOW. The only redeeming victim needs a catastrophic (>= 42%) loss plus an owner-ordered minter-first exit. Even then the asset loss is the vault loss itself. L-28 only makes the owner's totalWithdrawal report success misleadingly. That is incorrect state handling, which is QA/Low under C4. A redeemable user claim never passes through the no-op, because V2 does not use totalWithdrawal.
escalationTriggers: MEDIUM if a single redeeming client comes to hold principal >= ~95% of a strategy's D, so that a realistic (<5%) loss cap-binds, while a second client with a redeemable claim shares the vault.

MEDIUM if any automated migration/cutover script (phStaging2) treats WithdrawalExecuted or a successful totalWithdrawal as proof of delivery and then re-books or burns the client's principal downstream.
Re-weigh if a second REDEEMING (non-minter) client is authorized on the same strategy (the minter-cushion premise would fail).
classifications.notes: Metadata: the `contract` field should list both ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol and ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:214-217 (human, fingerprint unchanged). Disclose sibling L-13 1456259d8ac6. Do not collapse it.

classifications.change: none. The documented 'V2 wired => MEDIUM' trigger FIRED and was explicitly engaged. The escalation is declined on the evidence.

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated to co-clients, protocol surplus or phUSD supply. When the AMM bids above NAV, the exiter receives more underlying than the principal debited. The excess is funded by the AMM counterparty.
attackPath: 1. The sUSDe AMM price is above NAV.
2. A client exits. _disposeShares sells convertToShares(amount), the floored NAV-equivalent of the debited principal.
3. The AMM pays the premium. The exiter receives amount + premium.
4. Under V2: minted phUSD = target - delivered, with delivered capped at target, so 0 is minted. The excess is forwarded to the caller (StableStakerV2.sol:584-588).
classification.likelihood: The mechanism occurs whenever the pool trades at a premium. A HARM path is not demonstrated.
classification.assumptions: Dominance holds (I4 at all 589 cap-binds, I9 shares disposed <= convertToShares(a): PASS). The V2 underwater guard blocks V < D on the voluntary path. A sUSDe premium is arbitraged by a permissionless sUSDe.deposit.

classifications.probeEngagement: work/test/econ-run18/OverDeliveryConservation.t.sol 3/3 PASS: co-client NAV backing RISES (19,990.0e18 -> 20,006.7e18) and surplus is unchanged at a 5% premium. A fuzz over premium 1.00-1.10 and yield 0-2% never decreases either value. The trigger's premise ('over-crediting V2 is dilution') required the over-delivery to be paid from the commingled position or to mint phUSD. The probe shows it does neither. Remaining backing per principal (V - NAV(sold))/(D - amount) >= V/D whenever V >= D. The ledger note's claim of '+474e18 out of the commingled position' is refuted. The 474e18 comes from the AMM counterparty.
classifications.justification: Not Medium: no function or availability impact and no value leak from any protocol party. The premium is externally derived and the exiter's NAV entitlement is exact, so at most this is opportunity cost to the pot, which is out of scope by premise. It stays Low rather than QA because _withdrawInternal's NatSpec (:757-763) documents only the deficit direction, and the undocumented surplus direction is a spec/comment mismatch. That is honest Low/QA. Keeping the prior Low is the conservative choice and avoids a severity change without human sign-off.
classifications.borderlineReason: Low vs QA. A drop to QA is defensible. Do NOT escalate.
escalationTriggers: MEDIUM if any path disposes more shares than convertToShares(amount) (I9 breach) or cap-binds while V >= D (I4 breach). Either would make the commingled position fund the over-delivery.
MEDIUM if StableStakerV2 (or any consumer) is changed to credit, mint or re-stake against the full delivered amount instead of capping at target.
Re-weigh if the underlying/share pair becomes one without permissionless instant mint-arbitrage (the premium could persist and the skim/NAV relationship changes).
classifications.notes: Recommend the human correct the L-23 note (the claim that the over-delivery comes out of the commingled position is refuted) and remove the 'V2 => MEDIUM' trigger, replacing it with the triggers above.

classifications.faithfulnessRoute: spec-conformance (cross-repo): stable-staker story-028's rationale claims a bound ('the strategy's own slippageToleranceBps') that does not exist for ERC4626YieldStrategy. Route the rationale correction to the stable-staker lane.

classification.assetImpact: V2 mints unbacked phUSD for (target - delivered) on every DOLA/USDC autoAnnihilate, and the direct strategy has no delivery floor. Measured today: sDOLA has ~1 wei of rounding, and autoUSD has a static 1.38 bps discount. Both are dilution, but at dust scale and reward-bounded, and story-028 accepts this as design (exit slippage shifted to the protocol).
attackPath: 1. A V2 staker with owed reward calls autoAnnihilate(USDC). netWanted = min(owed reward, principal).
2. In the same tx/bundle the attacker depresses the autoUSD destination vaults' redeem output (UNVERIFIED leg).
3. The strategy calls vault.redeem with no min-assets, and delivery falls below convertToAssets.
4. V2 mints the shortfall as phUSD. The attacker unwinds the manipulation.
classification.likelihood: low / unverified. autoUSD idle is 707.5 USDC against a 16,358 USDC position, so exits above idle pull from destinations. Whether that pull is same-tx manipulable at a profit is not demonstrated. Extraction is capped per call by the reward-bounded netWanted.
classification.assumptions: (1) The Tokemak autopool redeem path delivers below convertToAssets when it pulls from destinations. (2) That delivery can be depressed within one tx. (3) The manipulation cost is below the extracted top-up. None of these is verified.
classification.externalRequirements: Tokemak destination-pool manipulability, plus enough owed reward to make extraction exceed cost

classifications.justification: The manipulable leg is unverified, so it is rated Low with its assumptions stated (be conservative). It is not dismissed, because the scope limit applies: phUSD minted through V2 is real dilution, and the only bound story-028 cites is absent here. The proven impact today is the static 1.38 bps per USDC exit, which is dust and accepted by design.
classifications.borderlineReason: Low vs Medium, depending on a fork probe that has not been run.
classifications.mediumTrigger: MEASURABLE: a mainnet fork probe at the current block shows that, for a redeem above autoUSD idle, the delivered USDC can be depressed by > 10 bps below convertToAssets through a same-tx action whose all-in cost (fees + unwind loss) is below 10 bps x the netWanted a single realistic V2 caller can request (total owed USDC-pool reward). Either condition alone does not trigger it. Also MEDIUM if any live direct-strategy target is replaced by a vault whose previewRedeem/convertToAssets gap exceeds ~10 bps (static discount minted as phUSD on every exit).
escalationTriggers: Re-weigh if V2 per-call top-up cap is removed/raised or netWanted becomes principal-bounded instead of reward-bounded.
classifications.notes: Disclose L-29 704404968a8f (same function, distinct root: missing measurement vs missing floor), ECON-A c50c08f9ee58, L-27 d9bd595066ef. Do not collapse.

classifications.change: none (consequence annotated: now an owner footgun bounding V2's phUSD top-up)

classification.assetImpact: slippageToleranceBps B is the only bound on unbacked phUSD that V2 mints per USDe autoAnnihilate (StableStakerV2.sol:494-499). At B, a self-sandwiching caller can capture roughly (B - natural gap) x netWanted, with minOut set by B. At B = MAX_BPS, minOut = 0 and the bound vanishes. The caller can then collect up to ~2x their owed reward (sandwich proceeds plus the phUSD top-up).
attackPath: 1. The sUSDe discount widens past B, and every USDe exit reverts (L-01 persistent variant / DEDUP-18-04).
2. The owner applies the natural fix and raises B via setSlippageTolerance (uncapped up to MAX_BPS).
3. A V2 staker with owed reward front-runs their own autoAnnihilate with a Curve dump, exits at depressed output above the new minOut, and back-runs.
4. V2 mints phUSD for target - delivered. The staker keeps the sandwich profit.
classification.likelihood: low at live parameters. At B = 30 the headroom is ~24 bps on a reward-bounded netWanted, against ~101 sUSDe of manipulation cost (CODE-001 fork data), which is unprofitable. V2's USDe principal is only 2,684 USDe, so the total extractable is bounded by the outstanding USDe-pool reward even at extreme B.
classification.assumptions: The owner raises B materially above the natural gap while outstanding owed rewards are material. The owner is non-malicious and is raising B only to unbrick exits.
classification.externalRequirements: A widened sUSDe discount (it triggers the owner action) plus enough reward balance to make extraction exceed cost

classifications.justification: This is a genuine Law-3 footgun. A competent owner editing a VAULT slippage knob to unbrick exits would be surprised that it raises the ceiling on phUSD any caller can extract, so it is in scope and must not be dropped. Classified by the impact it unlocks: a reward-bounded value leak that requires an owner action not yet taken and is unprofitable at live scale. That is Low today. It does not reach Medium because no harmful configuration exists (B = 30) and the per-call extraction is bounded by owed reward. Keep the existing fingerprint (same missing-cap root). A split for the downstream-mint consequence is a human choice.
classifications.borderlineReason: Low vs Medium. This is the highest-risk configuration hazard in the run, because its trigger is the remedy for another finding.
classifications.mediumTrigger: MEDIUM if setSlippageTolerance is ever called with B > ~100 bps (or > 3x the prevailing NAV-to-pool gap) on a strategy whose client is a phUSD-minting V2 while that pool's outstanding owed reward x (B - gap) exceeds the measured manipulation cost. Monitor SlippageToleranceSet events on 0xaC2e...7f95. HIGH-shaped only at B near MAX_BPS with material owed rewards (minOut = 0).
classifications.safeConfigGuidance: Cap B well below MAX_BPS in the setter. Document in the NatSpec/CLAUDE.md that B bounds V2's minted top-up. Runbook: when exits revert because the discount widened, pause autoAnnihilate on the stable-staker side, or bump B only briefly with autoAnnihilate disabled, instead of leaving B high.

classification.assetImpact: None at present: the live adapter's 2 RouteSet logs (blocks 25283690/1) are contiguous. If a future owner setRoute on the immutable live adapter 0x2D02 stores a gapped route (accepted by the legacy validator), Router NG stops at the first gap. The USDe strategy's deposit/withdraw/skim then revert (availability), or an intermediate token is delivered.
attackPath: 1. The owner reads HEAD source and believes setRoute enforces contiguity.
2. The owner sets a new route on the live adapter without off-chain validation against the story-052 rule.
3. The legacy validator accepts the gapped route.
4. Strategy swaps revert or mis-deliver until the route is overwritten.
classification.likelihood: low: it requires a future owner configuration action. It is recoverable by overwrite.
classification.assumptions: The owner is non-malicious and trusts the HEAD source (that surprise is what makes it a footgun).

classifications.justification: An operational hazard per Law 3: non-obvious, because HEAD's guarantee silently does not apply to the deployed bytecode. The realised impact would be a temporary availability loss on a live strategy, recoverable by overwrite, and it depends on a future owner action. That is Low. The Halmos PASS for S1-S4 applies to HEAD only, and the legacy validator fails all four.
escalationTriggers: MEDIUM if any RouteSet event beyond the 2 known appears on 0x2D02 without a recorded off-chain validation against the story-052 rule, or if a stored route on 0x2D02 fails S1-S4.
Compounds with DEDUP-18-10: AMMRoutes.json additions are not asserted by the routeGap test, so a new mainnet route has no automated contiguity check on either side.
classifications.safeConfigGuidance: Before any setRoute on 0x2D02, validate the route off-chain against S1-S4 (or redeploy the adapter and strategy). Note in src/CLAUDE.md that the live adapter predates the validator.

classification.assetImpact: None. A transient revert of a pending exit, skim or totalWithdrawal Phase-2. The attacker pays ~$127 per grief and gains nothing. No value-leak framing and no solvency framing (doNotReRaise: M-02 d7f6c2dfd580, M-02-run11 c7329862eb0e, M-01-run12 fdda8f53151a).
attackPath: 1. The victim's exit/skim/Phase-2 tx is in the public mempool.
2. The attacker front-runs it with a Curve pool dump that pushes output below NAV x (1 - B) (~23.8 bps of headroom under B = 30).
3. The victim's tx reverts on minOut. The attacker unwinds at a cost.
classification.likelihood: low. It is unprofitable, defeated by a private mempool, and the victim simply retries. Burning the 72h Phase-2 window would require griefing every attempt for 72h against private submission.

classifications.justification: Inherent to any slippage-guarded swap, transient, atomic (no partial state consumed), and with no profit motive. C4 treats this as QA. It is distinct from the closed MEV framings, because it claims a same-bundle revert, not a leak or a persistent decoupling. It is kept as a visible QA item per Law 1. Flag: the owner previously rejected MEV framings on this path, so the human should confirm whether a QA note is wanted.
classifications.borderlineReason: QA vs drop (owner precedent). Not Low/Medium.
escalationTriggers: LOW/MEDIUM if a revert can be made to consume a one-shot or time-bounded resource: for example, Phase-2 state reset before the swap without revert atomicity, or a V2 initiateMigration that cannot be retried privately.
Interacts with L-01/ECON-002: repeated griefing pressures the owner to raise B, which is the CLASS-18-04 footgun trigger. Prefer private submission to raising B.

classification.assetImpact: No asset loss. A route with swap_type >= 10 is stored, and every swap reverts until the route is overwritten. This freezes the market strategy's deposit/withdraw/skim (availability, owner-recoverable).
attackPath: 1. The owner sets a route with an out-of-range swap_type, trusting that the validator enforces validity.
2. The first swap reverts in Router NG.
3. The owner overwrites the route.
classification.likelihood: low. It needs an owner configuration error, it fails loudly on the first swap, and it is recoverable by overwrite.

classifications.justification: An owner-authored misconfiguration that fails loudly and is recoverable. The owner rated the analogous sya-harvester run-02 L-05 (swap_type >= 9) as QA, so this follows that precedent. It is kept visible as a Law-3 footgun, because the NatSpec implies swap_type validity is enforced.
escalationTriggers: LOW if an out-of-range swap_type is ever stored on a live adapter with clients unable to exit during the overwrite window (cf. DEDUP-18-03: the live adapter has the older validator).

classification.assetImpact: None directly. src/CLAUDE.md overstates the routeGap test's coverage: it parses two hard-coded keys, not every AMMRoutes.json route.
attackPath: n/a (documentation/test-coverage deviation)

classifications.justification: A pure behavioural/documentation deviation from story-052 with no security impact on its own. Per Law 2 it goes to the F-XX spec-conformance report, not the QA/gas bundle. It is cross-linked to DEDUP-18-03 because the false assurance matters most for routes that may be set on the live adapter, which lacks the validator.

otherReWeighs.label: L-29
otherReWeighs.justification: V2 live: V2 measures the balance delta itself (story-051), so the strategy discarding vault.redeem's return no longer feeds a consumer's sizing. The missing-floor consequence is filed separately as DEDUP-18-06. Stays Low.

otherReWeighs.label: ECON-A
otherReWeighs.justification: V2 live: fee-blind convertToAssets overstates autoUSD NAV by ~1.38 bps. That can let V2's _isUnderwater guard read 'above par' marginally when previewRedeem would read below, so a guarded exit proceeds and V2 mints the dust gap as phUSD (dilution, but dust and reward-bounded). Stays Low. MEDIUM trigger: same as DEDUP-18-06, a previewRedeem/convertToAssets gap > ~10 bps on a live direct-strategy target.

otherReWeighs.label: L-07
otherReWeighs.justification: The zero-gap half was closed at HEAD (Halmos S1-S4 PASS, unbounded). The tokenIn==tokenOut and coin-index residuals are owner-config, and CODE-003 shows they fail loudly on Router NG. Stays Low (a QA candidate after the narrowing; human). Note that the zero-gap half is NOT closed on the live adapter 0x2D02 (DEDUP-18-03).

otherReWeighs.label: L-02 (expired closure)
otherReWeighs.justification: The premise 'never more than 3 clients' is falsified (4 authorized). A 4-iteration loop is nowhere near a gas brick. The impact is unchanged. The human should re-affirm it with a gas-bound rationale or deauthorize V1.

observations.status: surfaced for human triage. NOT minted as a finding by the classifier.
observations.title: Owner-ordered exit of the revoked OLD minter's 58% USDe position while the strategy is below par shifts the commingled loss onto StableStakerV2 (inverts the minter-cushion direction)
observations.reasoning: The market strategy pays an exiter the NAV of the principal debited (convertToShares(amount)), so under a loss the FIRST exiter is made whole and the LAST exiters bear the whole loss (I4 dominance). The premise intends the non-redeeming minter to be V2's cushion. If the owner retires the revoked OLD minter (0x435B, 3,749.62 USDe) by withdrawing its position while V < D, V2 (the only redeeming client) absorbs the entire loss instead of sharing it, and V2 then emits Antimatter against under-backed principal (dilution, per the scope limit). A competent owner tidying up a revoked minter is unlikely to expect that the exit order decides who bears the loss. That surprise makes it a potential Law-3 footgun.
observations.suggestedSeverity: low (operational hazard) if the human agrees that it is in scope. Today the vault is not below par, and the action has not been taken.
observations.safeConfigGuidance: Withdraw the OLD minter's position only while totalBalance >= principal for the strategy, or only after V2 has exited or migrated.
related: memory: minter-cushion-socialized-losses-intended (not contradicted: this concerns exit ORDER, not the cap)
